olivia: Quick sync — we need to choose an internal API shape for routing/quotas/telemetry across hosted/dedicated/private.

olivia: Two concrete options on the table:
- shard-by-vertical: separate endpoints per product surface (chat, embeddings, rerank). Each shard owns its routing, quotas, telemetry.
- composable-shim: single gateway with plugin shims that assemble routes per caller and can apply policies dynamically.

sam: +1 to listing pros/cons. I worry about operational overhead of many shards.

raj: Shards are simple for per-vert SLAs and rate limits. Easier to reason about cost attribution. But cross-vert features (shared cache, KV reuse) get messy.

maria: Composable shim gives us centralized telemetry and consistent rollout semantics (canary per-route). But it adds runtime complexity and more surface area for bugs.

olivia: Major questions: rollout UX (can we canary a shim vs a shard?), quota enforcement (centralized vs distributed), and telemetry granularity (fine per-vert vs unified traces).

raj: For canarying: with shards we can do simple traffic split at infra level (weighting) -> clean. With shim you can canary plugin but need feature flags + fine routing rules.

jin: Infra note: composed gateway increases p95 latency unless optimized. We can do fast-paths (no plugin for hot routes) but it needs work in runtime.

maria: Observability tradeoff: with shards you get per-service dashboards out of box. With shim we need labels and consistent tagging to split by logical vert.

sam: Quotas: centralized quota service is easiest with shim; shards need global quota propagation (token buckets across services) which is complex.

infra-bot: deploy.bot: canary-deploy initiated by @olivia for branch internal-api/experimental-shim -> 5% traffic to staging cluster (link: https://deploys.redwood/1234)

olivia: Good. I'd like a prototype of the shim to validate latency + canary flow. If perf looks bad we revert to shard-first approach.

raj: Suggest a short spike: implement shim as a thin router that forwards to existing shard handlers (so we can compare added latency). Keep plugins disabled initially.

maria: Also add tracing headers and cost attribution tags in the spike: model, seq_len_bucket, shard_id, caller_team.

sam: Decision checklist for spike:
- measure p50/p95 added by shim
- implement centralized quota check stub
- prove canary route override (split by header)
- wire tracing to Tempo/Jaeger

olivia: Timeline: 1 week spike. If shim p95 overhead < 8ms and we get canary working, lean shim-first. Else shard-first.

jin: I'll provision infra for the spike (new small cluster + k8s ingress) and add flame probe. ETA EOD.

maria: I'll add an eval prompt set for telemetry and a couple of synthetic workloads (hot short chat, long generation, embeddings) to stress the shim.

raj: Sounds good. If anyone has objections call them out now. Otherwise I'll make a PR with router skeleton and perf test harness.

sam: No objections. @raj please include the quota propagation notes in the PR description.

olivia: OK moving forward. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: one more: if we choose shim-first, we'll need strong doc guidance for plugin authors (timeouts, side-effects, idempotency). Add to tech docs.

raj: noted.

infra-bot: alert.bot: new spike cluster ready -> https://k8s.redwood/spikes/shim-test (credentials in 1Password)

olivia: Great, closing thread. We'll reconvene after the spike results next Tues.
